chunks: It is narrated from al-Ala', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two Imams (peace be upon them)

Regarding a man who frees his male or female slave as a mudabbar (to be freed after his death) from himself, and then he needs the price of the slave: Does he sell him? He said: 'No, unless he stipulates to the one from whom he sells him that he must free him at the time of his death.'

key_terms.عَنْ دُبُرٍ: Conditional emancipation (tadbir), where a slave is freed upon the master's death
key_terms.عِنْدَ مَوْتِهِ: At the time of his death

ai.seo_question: Can a master sell a slave who has been conditionally freed (mudabbar) if he needs money before he dies?
ai.summary: This narration from *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih* clarifies the flexibility of *tadbir* (conditional emancipation) by allowing the master to sell the slave if financial need arises, provided the condition of emancipation upon the master's death is preserved for the buyer. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic view that the slave's right to freedom is attached to the master's death rather than being an immediate transfer of ownership, allowing for temporary commercial use while maintaining the ultimate goal of liberation.
